fields.acceptance: A Go test in internal/api builds a repo with a large log (100+ change sets, several in flight) and its index (IndexPath set), drives a run's leaves and checks steps through the stepRunner with live sessions, polls repeatedly with nothing changed and asserts, through the ctx.readLog counter and a fold counter, that those polls read the log zero times and fold nothing; it then adds a log entry and a session done mark and asserts the next poll sees both. A CPU budget test (quiettest, median, like TestReadBudget) measures the process CPU time of idle driver polls on the 50,000-node budget model and asserts each costs under 5 ms of CPU
fields.statement: A run driver's poll (agent, leaves and checks steps, and their arbiter waits) reads the model through the worktree's index, and a poll where the log's stat fingerprint, the run journal and the polled session records are unchanged does no model work: no log read, no decode and no fold

fields.acceptance: TestReadBudget times rhiza change show of an in-flight change set on the 50,000-node budget model under the 50 ms median; a Go test with a counting log reader and a fresh index asserts change show and ship check --settled read the log zero times; the existing change show and ship testscripts pass unchanged
fields.statement: rhiza change show and rhiza ship check --settled take the model and change sets from the worktree's index, caught up incrementally, instead of reading and folding the whole log, with the same answers as before

fields.acceptance: A Go test with a counting log reader and a fresh index asserts an apply of several writes reads the log zero times; a property test over generated logs and writes finds every write accepted or refused, with the same problems, through the index as through the full fold; a budget test times one rhiza apply write on the 50,000-node budget model under 200 ms median
fields.statement: rhiza apply (and the single-write commands add, set, link, retire, mv) validate a write against the index's folded state plus the write's own new entries, so a write never reads and folds the whole log; only rhiza check and rhiza render still read the whole log
